correctness.rationale: A finite monoid has unique greatest Green J-class consisting of the units; its divisibility arcs agree with the J-class order. In any root-oriented directed tree a strict upward class move cannot participate in a directed cycle. For each nonunit class of size \(w\), choosing \(k\) exits gives \(\binom wk\cdot k w^{w-k-1}\) internal rooted forests, with \(k=w\) counted as \(1\); summing with classwise external weight \(Q\) yields \(Q(wt+Q)^{w-1}\). The unit block contributes \(u^{u-2}t_U^{u-1}\). The product and its normalized probability generating function prove the full statement for every finite monoid. Recomputed exact Laplacian minors, direct enumeration for nine weighted/unweighted small posets, and direct Green-order tests of T2 and I2 match; these are finite checks only.

value.rationale: The object is a natural semigroup invariant introduced structurally in recent literature. The exact formula determines an entire multivariate class-edge arborescence polynomial for every finite monoid, including all noncommutative transformation and inverse monoids, without forming an enormous Laplacian. The stronger independent class-exit distribution is not implicit in a simple total count and provides an exact random-tree statistic; the rank-class examples have natural algebraic interpretations. The value is structural and quantitative, though the proof is short because its ingredients are classical.
